newsitem.title: USA: Lilly pleased by early Gemzar, Zyprexa sales.
newsitem.headline: Lilly pleased by early Gemzar, Zyprexa sales.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co president and chief operating officer Sidney Taurel said he is "very pleased" by early sales of two of its new products, Gemzar for pancreatic cancer and Zyprexa for treatment of schizophrenia.
"Sales of Gemzar are moving along at a strong clip and we're very pleased with its early acceptance," Taurel said at the Hambrecht and Quist health conference.

Early sales of Zyprexa are encouraging with U.S. doctors having written 100,000 prescriptions in the first 13 weeks since it came on the market. He said he expects Zyprexa to be approved for marketing in 60 countries by the end of 1997.
Lilly is also exploring expanded indications for the drug, including a potential treatment for bipolar disorder.
Taurel also said sales growth of its Prozac drug remained strong and is up about 17 percent year-to-date in the U.S.

He said the company also continues to boost overseas sales as a portion of total company sales. He said he expects overseas sales to account for at least half of company-wide revenues by the year 2000, up 44 percent from 1995 and 25 percent from 1985.
